body:
> is it documented somewhere - or can someone give me a hint - on how this HTMLTemplateAnalyzer needs to be configured so I can use it for php based view-templates/files?



> I also added a beforeAnalyzeFile hook to TysonAndre/psalm - that seems like it should be generally useful

That will be added in the linked PR. My plugin code wouldn't work without it. Then you just 

1. Update the regexes to suit your project and save the plugin in your project.

    (I don't know how you'd save plugin configs in psalm.xml - I guess you could put it's config in a separate file if you wanted it to be generic)
2. Add the relative path to the `<plugin>` to the `<plugins>` section of psalm.xml
Would the suggestion in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/issues/2032#issuecomment-522325571 be a better alternative then the mentioned plugin?

> Would the suggestion in 2032 (comment) be a better alternative then the mentioned plugin?

That depends on the use case. psalm-this-var is definitely more widely usable and useful to have (I forget if psalm has something similar for closures, along the lines of `@phan-closure-scope`)

For example, if you have hundreds of files where `$this` is `MyTemplateClass` in one folder, then it's repetitive and error-prone to type that in hundreds of files, so there's still use cases for this.
@muglug our framework has the very same semantics. Would be great to know how to configure psalm for that case

> Would be great to know how to configure psalm for that case

Use the `TemplateChecker` plugin with a `/** @variablesfrom Foo\Bar::baz` annotation in your template

_although_

Vimeo's views are also neatly separated by file extension:

```xml
    <fileExtensions>
        <extension name=".php"/>
        <extension name=".phtml" scanner="path/to/TemplateScanner.php" checker="path/to/TemplateChecker.php"/>
    </fileExtensions>
```

Not sure how it would work for you - the hook I just merged from @TysonAndre may be necessary
